key_insight: PathAgentBench shows that pathology VLMs can reason well over curated evidence, but struggle to find that evidence directly in whole-slide images.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights a major gap for AI tools intended to support pathology workflows: accurate diagnosis requires both identifying relevant regions and integrating findings across magnifications.
method: Built a diagnostic-tree benchmark linking nested regions across magnifications to scale-specific findings and final diagnoses.
Evaluated 20 general-purpose, medical, and pathology-specialized models on image-text matching, text-image retrieval, region localization, and multi-scale reasoning.
Added a private breast cancer cohort to test autonomous whole-slide exploration.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 1,822 TCGA WSIs, 17,135 diagnostic paths, and 190 private breast cancer WSIs annotated by ten board-certified pathologists.
watch_item: Autonomous slide exploration remains weak, with very low high-magnification hit rates, so benchmark performance may not translate to reliable real-world slide navigation.
paper_title: PathAgentBench: Benchmarking Evidence-Seeking Vision-Language Models on Whole-Slide Pathology Image
